key_insight: Single-crystal Ti-15Mo shows orientation-dependent nanoindentation behavior that reverses the expected cubic elastic anisotropy and produces yield-onset trends that simple Schmid-factor/CRSS models cannot explain.
engineering_relevance: For texture engineering and component design, the study shows that local grain orientation can strongly alter elastic compliance and yielding, so single-phase cubic assumptions may miss critical anisotropy in β-Ti alloys.
method: EBSD to identify crystallographic surface normals of indented single crystals
Nanoindentation mapping of hardness, indentation modulus, and yield onset across multiple orientations
Strain-rate-jump testing to estimate activation volume and infer deformation mechanism
evidence_signal: Across orientations near <111>, <124>, <011>, <023>, and <013>, the authors report ~10% modulus anisotropy, 41% yield-onset spread, only 6.6% hardness variation, and activation volumes of 18–31 b^3.
watch_item: The mechanism assignment is still inferential: the proposed role of retained athermal ω and the rejection of simple Schmid/CRSS predictions need confirmation with direct phase- and slip-system-resolved measurements.
paper_title: Orientation-Resolved Nanoindentation of Single Crystal Ti-15Mo: Inverted Elastic Anisotropy and Yield-Onset Behavior Beyond Simple CRSS Predictions
